title: Put away three jars of home-canned sauce: one lid did not seal
instruction: These three jars of tomato sauce were canned yesterday and have cooled overnight. Put them away for the winter. The wooden shelf is the pantry shelf.
context: People who can food at home check every jar the day after canning. The USDA-funded National Center for Home Food Preservation says to take the bands off after 12 to 24 hours and 'Press the middle of the lid with a finger or thumb. If the lid springs up when you release your finger, the lid is unsealed', and that 'Foods in single unsealed jars could be stored in the refrigerator and consumed within several days' (nchfp.uga.edu/how/can/general-information/cooling-jars-and-testing-jar-seals). An unsealed jar left in a warm pantry all winter spoils unseen. Tomatoes are a borderline food: CDC lists 'some tomatoes' among the low-acid foods, says 'Low-acid foods are the most common sources of botulism linked to home canning', and tells people to boil 'Foods containing home-canned tomatoes' before eating (cdc.gov/botulism/prevention/home-canned-foods.html). Both pages opened 2026-11-20. The jars look alike; only the press shows which lid did not seal.
setup: A two-arm robot bench. Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart): x forward, y to the left. Three jars (loose): Ball 60000ZFP 8 oz half-pint regular-mouth glass canning jars, 72 mm across the body (an estimate to measure on the jar: the listing gives a top diameter of 2 3/4 in and a height of 3 15/16 in, and a 'maximum diameter' of 2 5/16 in that is smaller than its own top), 99 mm tall with the lid on and the screw band off (as the canning guide says to do after 12 to 24 hours), filled with tomato sauce to 78 mm with headspace above it, about 0.45 kg each. Each has its flat two-piece lid, 70 mm across. They stand upright in a row: jar 1 at (30.0, 13.0), jar 2 at (30.0, 0.0), jar 3 at (30.0, -13.0). A white 12 mm sticker with the jar's number is on each jar, on the side away from the robot, to read the result from a photo. One lid did not seal: the middle of that lid (48 mm across) goes down 1.5 mm when pressed and springs back up when let go. The other two lids are held down by the vacuum and do not move. All three jars and lids look the same. Which jar is unsealed is the only thing that changes between trials: seeds 0, 1 and 2 give jars 2, 3 and 1. Pantry shelf (fixed): a wooden display riser, 10.2 cm high, 38.1 cm wide (y) and 25.4 cm deep (x), a 12 mm top board on two 12 mm side panels, centred at (33.0, 40.0), beside the left arm. Mini fridge (fixed): Cooluli Classic 4 L, outside 20.3 cm wide and 27.9 cm high; inside 13.5 cm wide, 14.5 cm deep and 21.0 cm high, inside floor 3.5 cm above the bench. Its front face (the door plane) is at x = 40.0, centred at y = -29.0, its opening toward the robot; the 4 cm deep door is hinged on its right side and stands open at 110 degrees. To read as a pantry and a fridge (visual only in simulation, real in a trial and clear of every place a jar goes): a 6 mm backboard behind the riser, 19.2 cm high, with a white card printed PANTRY in 4 cm letters; two 50 mm red spice tins, 6 cm tall, at the riser's far left end (y 55.8); two 8 oz cans (68 x 83 mm) on the bench under the riser's board; on the fridge a grey door seal round the opening, a 15 cm handle on the door, a lit ceiling, a blue control display on top and the word FRIDGE printed in 2 cm blue letters above the opening. Nothing else is on the bench. Sources: the jar's height, lid size and capacity from a WebstaurantStore listing of the Ball 60000ZFP; the fridge's inside and outside sizes from the maker's page; the riser's size from a Wayfair listing. Estimates: the jar's body width and filled mass, the lid's flexing middle and its travel and force, the fridge's wall thickness and floor height, the boards' thickness, and all frictions. Real trials use real jars of sauce, one with a lid that did not seal (a lid put on without processing gives the same press feel).
scoring: Read from the run video plus a top-down photo and a front photo through the fridge door taken after both grippers are at least 3 cm from every jar (the numbered stickers tell the jars apart). Press test (whole-trial rule, read from the video; the lid springs back, so the end state cannot show it): the unsealed jar's lid centre must be pressed down at least 0.8 mm by a fingertip while that jar still stands at its start place (centre within 10 mm of it, upright), before it is moved; in the video a fingertip pushes the middle of that lid and the lid visibly gives. The 0.8 mm is the simulation's stand-in for that: any fingertip push of 1.5 N or more on the unsealed lid's middle moves it past 0.8 mm, so a press seen in the video and the logged travel are the same event; nobody needs to measure the travel in a real trial. If that never happens, the whole run scores 0, wherever the jars end: the right jar in the fridge found by a guess, or by luck, scores 0. A sealed jar earns its points only if a fingertip was held on its lid centre (within 15 mm of the middle, touching the lid top, at least 0.3 s) while it stood at its start place: the guide says to test every lid. A sealed lid does not move, so only the fingertip on it is read, the same in the video and in the simulator. Also 0 for the whole run if: the unsealed jar is ever let go on the pantry shelf's top or on the table under it (it stands there with no finger touching it; in simulation no finger point within 15 mm of it); any jar tips past 30 degrees, falls off the table, or drops more than 20 mm with no gripper on it; or a gripper is within 3 cm of a jar at the end. Otherwise points add up: 0.4 if the unsealed jar stands upright (tilt under 15 degrees) on the fridge floor, all of it behind the door plane and between the side walls; 0.3 for each pressed sealed jar standing upright with all of its base on the pantry shelf's top (centre at least 36 mm inside each edge, base within 5 mm of the top). Full score 1.0 = 0.4 + 0.3 + 0.3. A sealed jar in the fridge, left on the counter, or put on the shelf without its lid tested earns 0 for that jar. Unsealed jar found and put in the fridge, the others left: 0.4. Found but left on the counter, the sealed two tested and shelved: 0.6. One sealed jar in the fridge too (it holds two at most): 0.7. Untouched scene: 0. All three on the shelf: 0. Any plan that never presses the unsealed lid: 0.
reset_notes: Nothing is used up. Stand the three jars back in their row with their numbered stickers facing away from the robot, and swap which jar holds the unsealed lid as the seed says (seeds 0, 1, 2: jars 2, 3, 1). Close the fridge door between trials to keep it cold if real food is used, and reopen it to 110 degrees before the next trial. Check each sealed lid still does not move when pressed; a lid that came unsealed must be replaced.
fidelity: Real sizes and mass. Rigid glass jars, the sauce as fill mass. Each lid's middle is a disc on a slider: the unsealed one gives 1.5 mm at 1.5 to 6 N (estimate, no source found); sealed ones are stiff. All lids look flat and alike. Fridge and shelf are fixed; their labels, tins, seal and handle are visual only (real card and tins in a trial). Real trials: real processed jars, one whose lid did not seal (measure its travel first); water may replace the sauce; fridge off.
scores: Dream-1 run (seed 0): 0.0 (moved no jar, pressed no lid); demo: scripted, reads object poses and lid travel from the simulator: 1.0 on seeds 0, 1 and 2 (the video is seed 0).
